subject: FluxCart: Large regional latency surge — confirmation & compensation request
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@fluxcart.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood-inference.com
Cc: support+ops@fluxcart.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: Latency spike impacting checkout (3/31 22:10-4/1 02:30 UTC)

Hi Kimberly,

We observed a severe latency spike that impacted our checkout API (POST /v1/cart/complete) starting 2029-03-31 22:10 UTC and lasting until roughly 2029-04-01 02:30 UTC. During the window we saw 25–40% of requests > 4s and a small number of 5xxs. This resulted in ~3.4% revenue loss for that hour on our side (preliminary).

Can you confirm whether this aligns with Redwood's telemetry for region us-west-2, and whether this is eligible for SLA compensation per our contract? We need:
- confirmed downtime/latency window (start/end)
- classification (availability vs latency tail breach)
- evidence bundle and any postmortem invite times

We're in a tight procurement cycle and will need an eligibility estimate by EOD tomorrow. I can attach our request-ids if that helps.

Thanks,
Anjali Rao
Head of Ops, FluxCart
anjali@fluxcart.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 16:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting checkout (3/31 22:10-4/1 02:30 UTC)

Hi Anjali — we're looking at the traces now. Summary of what we've found so far: 

1) Redwood telemetry (sampled traces + tokenized request logs) shows an elevated P99 for the FluxCart tenant in us-west-2 starting ~2029-03-31T22:08:45Z and returning to baseline ~2029-04-01T02:28:30Z. That matches your window closely.

2) Root cause (prelim): an autoscaler coordination loop triggered by a faulty health-check in a subset of serving pods. The autoscaler performed repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles which caused transient queueing and tail latency. We also observed a small number of capacity preemption events from the underlying host pool during the window.

3) Classification: This appears to be a latency tail SLO breach for the configured checkout route rather than a full service outage (ie, availability SLO not entirely violated). Per your contract (SLA section 4.2), latency tail breaches that exceed the monthly threshold are eligible for proportional credits.

I've attached an evidence bundle (two files): fluxcart-traces-20290401.zip (sampled traces + request-id mapping), and slo-uptime-snapshot-20290401.csv (per-route SLO aggregates). Attachments: fluxcart-traces-20290401.zip (log bundle, 8.2MB); slo-uptime-snapshot-20290401.csv (CSV, 45KB).

Provisional credit estimate: based on the measured exceeded tail across the impacted one-hour window we estimate a proportional credit between 6–12% of the monthly invoice for that billing period. Final credit requires agreement on the exact window and confirmation of multi-tenant impact (we show FluxCart specifically affected).

Proposed next steps: 
- Kimberly will coordinate a 60-min postmortem with your team and our infra/serving leads. Proposed window: Tue 2029-04-02 16:00–17:00 UTC (I will send a calendar invite).
- If you prefer earlier, we can do Tue 2029-04-02 09:00–10:00 PDT.

Please confirm which time works and attach any additional request-ids you want included in the trace slice.

Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting checkout (3/31 22:10-4/1 02:30 UTC) — postmortem invite + artifacts

Hi Anjali / Kimberly / Karthik,

Thanks for confirming the request IDs — we've ingested them and re-ran the slice. Confirmed final impactful window: 2029-03-31T22:08:37Z -> 2029-04-01T02:28:31Z. Evidence bundle is uploaded to the shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-trace-id (contains full sampled traces, kernel-level scheduling events, and the SLO snapshot CSV).

Calendar invite sent for:
- Postmortem: Tue 2029-04-02 16:00–17:00 UTC (attendees: FluxCart ops + Redwood infra + Serving team).

Preliminary remediation actions we're committing to: 
- Hotfix applied to autoscaler health-check logic (deployed 2029-04-01T06:12:00Z UTC).
- Host pool preemption policy adjusted to prefer draining over immediate preemption for short-running inference shards (applied 2029-04-01T09:30:00Z UTC).
- We will produce a formal RCA doc within 72 hours and a finalized credit calculation within 5 business days after the postmortem.

Provisional credit range (for planning): 6–12% of the impacted month invoice. Final credit will be calculated per contract with exact window and customer traffic fraction applied.

Attachments: fluxcart-traces-20290401.zip (log bundle, 8.2MB); slo-uptime-snapshot-20290401.csv (CSV, 45KB)

Best regards,
